formalizations.formalization: ∀ (a : Point) (b : Point) (c : Point) (d : Point) (e : Point) (f : Point) (AB : Line) (CD : Line) (EF : Line), ((distinctPointsOnLine a b AB) ∧ (distinctPointsOnLine c d CD) ∧ (distinctPointsOnLine e f EF) ∧ (¬(AB.intersectsLine EF)) ∧ (¬(CD.intersectsLine EF))) → (¬(AB.intersectsLine CD))
formalizations.full_output: theorem example_thm (a b c d e f : Point) (AB CD EF : Line) (h1 : distinctPointsOnLine a b AB) (h2 : distinctPointsOnLine c d CD) (h3 : distinctPointsOnLine e f EF) (h4 : ¬(AB.intersectsLine EF)) (h5 : ¬(CD.intersectsLine EF)) : ¬(AB.intersectsLine CD) := by

reference_formalization: ∀ (AB CD EF : Line), AB ≠ CD ∧ CD ≠ EF ∧ EF ≠ AB ∧ ¬(AB.intersectsLine EF) ∧ ¬(CD.intersectsLine EF) → ¬(AB.intersectsLine CD)
nl_statement: (Straight-lines) parallel to the same straight-line are also parallel to one another.Let each of the (straight-lines) $AB$ and $CD$ be parallel to $EF$. I say that $AB$ is also parallel to $CD$. <prf>  Thus, $AB$ is parallel to $CD$ [Prop.~1.27]. Thus, (straight-lines) parallel to the same straight-line are also parallel to one another.
